full_judgment: In the case of Thakur Singh vs Bhogeraj Singh, 'reported in ILR 27 (Cal) 29 their Lordships held that "in order to acquire title by adverse possession, the possession must not only be open and exclusive, but it must also be shown to have been adverse for the full statutory period i-e, it must be continuous for the full period (without any break or without interruption)." And as per decision given in the case of Badri vs Smt. Ram Rati, 1977 RD (BR) 224, it was held that the claimant has to specifically show his possession from year to year, particularly so, if he is a trespasser by continuity. " (also the case of Gouri Sanker vs Deputy Director, Consolidation, 1980 RD 250 continuity not found, presumption not drawn). In another case of Ganda Singh and others vs Ram Narain Singh, reported in AIR 1959 (Punjab) 147 it was held that "the claimant must show on what date he came into possession, what was the nature of his possession, whether the factum of his possession was known to the legal claimants and how long his possession continued."
